message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"12.18","text":"And, so that I do not prolong for you words that are unnecessary, I lived with her because of her devotion to her husband. Before long, my hands—wretched woman that I am—were paralyzed by attacks of biting pain, and the woman who had taken me in, her whole body bound by some affliction, lies prostrate at home. Since, then, the compassion of the women from before has waned, and both I and the woman at home are incapacitated, for many years I have sat here, as you see, begging; and whatever I manage to obtain, I also carry home for my fellow sufferer’s sustenance. So much for my own affairs; let them have been told sufficiently. What remains is that you are preventing the fulfillment of your promise to give me the drug, so that I may give it to her as well, since she desires to die, and in this way I too may be able to depart from life, as you said.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"διὰ τὴν φιλανδρίαν","chosen":"because of her devotion to her husband","rationale":"φιλανδρία denotes love of or devotion to a husband. The immediate context favors the poor widow’s devotion, though the phrase could encompass the narrator’s corresponding marital devotion."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τῶν δηγμάτων παρείθησαν","chosen":"were paralyzed by attacks of biting pain","rationale":"δήγματα literally denotes bites or stings and can describe sharp, biting pains; a more literal alternative is “were disabled by the bites.”"},{"source_quote":"ὅλη ὑπὸ πάθους τινὸς συνδεθεῖσα","chosen":"her whole body bound by some affliction","rationale":"ὅλη indicates that the affliction affected her wholly, while συνδεθεῖσα retains the image of being bound."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκίας ἔρριπται","chosen":"lies prostrate at home","rationale":"The perfect ἔρριπται presents the resulting prostrate condition as continuing at the time of the woman’s account; “has been laid prostrate at home” is another possible rendering."},{"source_quote":"ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ ἡ κατ’ οἶκον ἀμφότεραι ἐπισινεῖς τυγχάνομεν","chosen":"both I and the woman at home are incapacitated","rationale":"The present τυγχάνομεν describes both women as currently harmed, impaired, or afflicted, explaining their continuing need."},{"source_quote":"ὧν ἂν εὐπορήσω","chosen":"whatever I manage to obtain","rationale":"εὐπορέω here concerns securing available resources rather than being generally wealthy."},{"source_quote":"καὶ τῇ συνταλαιπώρῳ εἰς τροφὰς κομίζω","chosen":"I also carry home for my fellow sufferer’s sustenance","rationale":"εἰς τροφὰς expresses the purpose of what she brings—providing nourishment or sustenance—without requiring that everything obtained be edible."},{"source_quote":"τὸ φάρμακον","chosen":"the drug","rationale":"φάρμακον can mean medicine, drug, or poison. “Drug” preserves the lexical breadth, while the expressed desire for death supplies the lethal purpose in context."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ζῆν ... μεταλλάξαι","chosen":"depart from life","rationale":"The construction is a euphemism for dying, literally involving a change or departure from living."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
